page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 480 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix calculations. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i-flex.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core operations, software compilation, image processing, and text processing. Static web serving throughput is also highly rated, reaching 103.58 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression and database operations perform in the top 25 percent, supported by a read-only memory bandwidth of 192.31 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, single-core CPU stress tests and large-block memory write speeds align with average tier performance, indicating a relative tradeoff in write-heavy memory operations compared to read-heavy workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i-flex family provides a balanced resource density for memory-intensive applications without the premium of local NVMe storage. The inclusion of AMX instructions enables efficient CPU-based LLM inference, with prompt processing speeds reaching 290.6 tokens/sec on medium-sized 7B models. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and read-heavy web serving infrastructures.
